reason: Base UI draws Checkbox and Radio as a span, so shadcn's disabled:opacity-50 (a :disabled selector) never matches and a disabled control stays fully opaque upstream; foundation reads [data-disabled] instead, which is what the utility means. An upstream defect, not a luma value.

The preset is generated with rtl:false, so its paddings and radii are physical (pl-/pr-, rounded-l-) and do not mirror under dir=rtl; the layer-3 rules are logical. The section proves DirectionProvider renders, not a value.

A preset app's globals.css carries no .cn-* rules, so the cn-input-otp class the shadcn component keeps is unstyled there; style-luma.css's `.cn-input-otp { gap-2 }` is luma's value and luma keeps it.

The shortcuts contain ⌘, which is in neither Inter build: the reference app falls back through next/font's Inter Fallback and the preview through Inter Variable plus the Pretendard Hangul fallback, so the glyph advance differs (0.3–1.8px, larger where a row holds two such glyphs). Font stack, not a value.

Dark mode only: Tailwind sorts luma's dark: colours (dark:bg-transparent on the outline button, dark:aria-invalid:border-destructive/50 on the checkbox) after the state utilities that have no dark counterpart (aria-expanded:bg-muted, aria-invalid:aria-checked:border-primary), so upstream an open outline trigger and an invalid checked checkbox lose their state colour in dark. luma keeps the state colours; reproducing the ordering would delete the signal.
